chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Playing violin for Duke in Check and Double Check
summary: The film makers demanded violins, Ellington found Royal at the Apex, and Royal played violin parts in the 1930 picture.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You told me off the tape, not on the tape, about how you happened to work with Duke in 1930 in "Check and Double Check."

Yeah, well, that was one of the ironies of big business. When the people brought Duke Ellington out here to do the music and to work in "Check and Double Check," all they were thinking about was the extravaganzas of movies and everybody thought in the big ways, like Louis B. Mayer, if

he was going to do a picture, he didn't think it would be correct unless they had at least 50 people doing the music behind the scenes and as long as it was big, a lot of times they figures big was good. So when Ellington came out here with about 12 pieces or however many people in his band, well, immediately, the people that were running the show out there -- I can't think of the name of the company. I believe it was RKO or something, where we made that picture in those years -- they says, "Oh, you have to have some violins and things along with your band." They didn't know nothing about Duke Ellington Band. Somebody had sold them a pig in a poke.

So, Duke says, "Yeah, if you want some violins, you can have some violins." But Duke Ellington had been known before that, two or three years before that, as being the Jungle Band and there wasn't no violins in the jungle.

So, there wasn't any horns in the jungle, really, you know? But he said, "Okay, you can get some violins." So, he started scrambling around town, trying to find some black violin players. So, luckily somebody told him, said, "That little Marshal Royal boy can play violins." So, they found me down at the Apex, which was next door to the Dunbar Hotel, the Somerville Hotel at that time, where Duke was staying, where everybody of note in -- that was black stayed when they came to town, was that one hotel.

So, he came down and told me that he would like to have me play the violin on Check and Double Check. // So, we went out there and he wrote out some violin parts and things and we played the violin parts. They probably cut it out. I don't remember whether they cut the violin parts out of the score or whether it was actually in the picture or not. But that was my introduction to Duke Ellington as a violin player. So, I actually was supposed to have gone back with the Ellington band later on around the mid-'30s as a violin player and a saxophone player, but instead of that, he hired two men. He hired Ben Webster as the saxophone player and he hired Ray Nance as a violin-trumpet player. So, I didn't go back to that. I wasn't --
